items.description: Each entry is one argv element, NOT a shell program: command substitution ($(...), backticks) and process substitution (<(...), >(...)) are REJECTED, by this schema and by the runner at load. A manifest carrying a shell program cannot be checked, tested, or reviewed -- every character is escaped twice and no linter can see it. Put the logic in a .sh file next to the manifest, COPY it into the image, and call that (e.g. ["sh", "run.sh"], or use the script field). Plain $VAR / ${VAR} references are fine.

context.description: The status context string (e.g. "ci/deploy"). Required when enabled is true.

target_url.description: Optional URL linked from the GitHub status check.

file.description: Script file path, relative to the hook or manager directory. Must resolve inside that directory -- a symlink escaping it is a load error.

interpreter.description: Interpreter that runs the file. Must be installed in the image (the Dockerfile bakes the code in; nothing is mounted).

A manifest carrying a shell program cannot be checked, tested, or reviewed -- every character is escaped twice and no linter can see it. Put the logic in a .sh file next to the manifest, COPY it into the image, and call that (e.g. ["sh", "run.sh"], or use the script field). Plain $VAR / ${VAR} references are fine.

args.description: Additional arguments passed after the script path.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for {"eq": ...}: the path/header must stringify to exactly this value.

eq.description: Matches a leaf whose stringified value equals this exactly.

ne.description: Matches a leaf whose stringified value differs. A missing path does NOT match (absence is not inequality).

in.description: Matches a leaf whose stringified value equals any listed value.

exists.description: true matches when the path resolves to anything (header present); false when it does not.

prefix.description: Matches a leaf whose stringified value starts with this.

regex.description: Matches a leaf containing a match of this Go (RE2 — linear-time, no backtracking) pattern; anchor with ^ and $ for a full match. Compiled at load time — a non-compiling pattern fails validation.

oneOf.description: Operator object; when several operators are set, all must accept (AND).

description: Configuration for a webhook-runner hook. Place this file as hook.json inside a named directory under the hooks root, next to the mandatory Dockerfile that bakes the hook's code into its image.

$schema.description: URI of the JSON Schema this hook.json is validated against. Set it to https://sites.pazer.build/webhook-runner/branch/master/hook.schema.json (the legacy https://wow-look-at-my.github.io/webhook-runner/hook.schema.json is still accepted, but serves frozen 2026-07-15 content).

api_key.description: API key for bearer-token authentication. Checked against the X-API-Key header (or api_key_header). May reference a secret as ${NAME}, resolved from the hook's sops-encrypted secrets.sops.env first, then the runner host's environment; if the reference is unresolvable the hook fails closed (all requests rejected). Recommended for most hooks.

api_key_header.description: HTTP header to read the API key from. Default: X-API-Key.

command.description: Optional override of the image's CMD, passed to docker run after the image name. Every hook runs the image webhook-runner builds from the Dockerfile in its directory (tagged by content hash) — code is baked in and immutable per run; when command is omitted, the image's CMD/ENTRYPOINT runs.

concurrency_group.description: Name of a concurrency group declared in concurrency.json at the hooks root. At most that group's limit of runs (counted across every hook sharing the group) execute at once; the rest queue as 'pending' with their timeout not yet counting. Referencing a group not declared in concurrency.json is a load/validation error. Omit for unbounded concurrency.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this hook does.

dind.description: When true, run the hook's container with the privileges to host its OWN nested container daemon: the runner adds --privileged and an anonymous volume at /var/lib/docker (--mount type=volume,dst=/var/lib/docker), applied identically on the live-run and `webhook-runner test` paths. The nested daemon's storage lives on that real volume because an inner overlay driver cannot stack on the outer container's overlay rootfs; --rm auto-removes the anonymous volume so inner storage never leaks between runs. The host's docker daemon is NEVER exposed — no docker socket is mounted, and the nested daemon is isolated from it. This is an AUDITED, host-root-equivalent capability (--privileged grants effectively full access to the host): enable it only for trusted, operator-curated hooks. Default: false.

enable.description: The hook's DEFAULT enabled state. When false, the hook loads disabled: deliveries are rejected (503) and scheduled runs are skipped exactly as if the operator kill switch were off, until an operator explicitly enables it. The dashboard/admin runtime override (POST /hooks/{id}/enable|disable, persisted server-side) always takes precedence over this default, in both directions. Absent = enabled, so existing hooks are unchanged.

github_status.description: GitHub commit status updates for this hook's runs: when a delivery's payload carries a repo + head SHA, the runner posts 'pending' as the run starts and 'success'/'error' when it finishes. A run with no commit to point at posts nothing.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration (e.g. "5m"): kill the run once the container has produced no output (stdout or stderr) for this long. Any output byte resets the idle clock. Arms at container launch -- after the concurrency-group slot is acquired -- so a queued run never idles out. Independent of timeout (the absolute ceiling); both may be set, and whichever fires first ends the run with status "timeout" (an idle kill carries a distinguishable "idle timeout ... (no output)" error message). Omit for no idle limit.

networks.description: Docker networks to attach the container to.

public_key.description: Base64 or hex-encoded Ed25519 public key. When set, incoming requests must include a valid Ed25519 signature of the body in the signature header.

run_title.description: Template for the friendly display title of this hook's runs, shown by the dashboard in place of the opaque run id (e.g. "{{repository.full_name}}#{{pull_request.number}}" renders "wow-look-at-my/go-toolchain#47"). A {{...}} placeholder names a dotted path into the parsed JSON payload ("pull_request.number", array elements by numeric index) or a request header via the "header:" prefix — exactly skip_if's key syntax and bounded traversal. Resolution is graceful and never blocks a run: each placeholder becomes the scalar leaf's string form (numbers as their JSON literal, true/false as those words); a missing path, an object/array, and JSON null become empty; when EVERY placeholder resolves empty the run simply gets no title (consumers fall back to the run id), otherwise pure-separator literals stranded next to empty placeholders are dropped and whitespace collapses. A template with no placeholders is a static title, always set. Resolved once at run creation, before skip_if — skipped runs are titled too; schedule-triggered runs resolve against the synthetic schedule payload and fall back to "schedule". Titles are capped at 200 characters, and a state hook can rename its run mid-flight via POST /title on the state API. A malformed template (unterminated "{{", empty "{{}}") is a load/validation error.

schedule.description: Go duration (e.g. "5m", "1h") to fire this hook on a fixed interval, in addition to any HTTP trigger. A scheduled run goes through the same pipeline as an HTTP-triggered one (tracked, gated by concurrency_group, KV-enabled, shown on the dashboard) with a synthetic payload marking it schedule-triggered. On startup, and whenever the schedule is newly added or its interval changes, the hook fires immediately, then every interval; the scheduler skips a tick while a previous run of the same hook is still in flight (skip-if-already-running). Omit for HTTP-triggered only.

script.description: Run a script file from the hook directory: derives the container command as <interpreter> <file> [args...]. Like all hook code, the script is baked into the hook's image by its Dockerfile (never mounted), so the interpreter must be installed in that image. An explicit command overrides the derived one.

seccomp.description: Narrow the container's syscall filter. Absent means the default: docker's builtin seccomp profile, unmodified. The block names specific relaxations -- there is deliberately no way to point at an arbitrary profile or to say 'unconfined'. seccomp.userns (default false): allow the container to create unprivileged USER NAMESPACES, by running it under docker's default profile plus an ungated allow for unshare/clone/clone3/setns (the default permits those only for a container holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which a hook container does not have; every other syscall keeps the default policy). seccomp.systempaths (default absent; the only accepted value is "unconfined") clears docker's MaskedPaths and ReadonlyPaths for the container. These are SEPARATE opt-ins because they widen different things, and an in-container sandbox needs BOTH: the kernel refuses a fresh procfs mount inside a user namespace while anything obscures the container's own /proc, and docker masks parts of it in every container, so with userns alone bubblewrap creates its namespace and then fails on the first mount with "Can't mount proc on /newroot/proc". The trade runs both ways: the hook gains the ability to sandbox its OWN workload, at the cost of a wider kernel surface for the container itself. userns: unprivileged user namespaces have a real CVE history. systempaths: /proc/sysrq-trigger becomes writable (a host reboot, for a process running as root), as does /proc/irq, and /proc/sched_debug and /proc/timer_list disclose host processes and kernel addresses even to an unprivileged process in a PID namespace. Neither adds a capability, so /proc/kcore (CAP_SYS_RAWIO) and most of /proc/sys (CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the init userns) stay refused, and the pair remains strictly narrower than dind's --privileged. AUDITED opt-ins like dind: enable only for trusted, operator-curated hooks. Applied identically on the live-run and `webhook-runner test` paths.

secret.description: Legacy: shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. Prefer api_key or public_key.

settings.description: The hook's OWN configuration: any JSON object shape it wants. webhook-runner never interprets it -- it validates the object against the settings.schema.json shipped next to this manifest (declaring settings without that file is a load error) and hands it to the container as a read-only file at $HOOK_SETTINGS_FILE. This replaced the `env` block, which mixed hook-private config into the runner's own parsed keys, forced every value to be a string, and was validated by nobody. Settings are read per RUN, so changing them takes effect on the next run without rebuilding the image. REFERENCES: a string value may contain ${settings:a.b[2].c} (another value in this same document) or ${env:NAME} (a variable from the entity's secrets.sops.env, then the runner host's environment). ${settings:...} resolves at LOAD, so the schema validates the RESOLVED value and a bad path is a load error; a whole-string reference keeps the referenced value's type. ${env:NAME} resolves when the container starts -- an unresolvable one FAILS THE RUN rather than becoming an empty string -- so at load the schema sees the reference text, and a field meant to hold one must permit it (e.g. anyOf with a ^\\$\\{env: pattern). Credentials belong here only under the same private-repo posture as the rest of the manifest; the admin API exposes the top-level KEY NAMES only.

signature_header.description: HTTP header containing the signature. Default: X-Signature-Ed25519 for public_key auth, X-Hub-Signature-256 for legacy HMAC.

skip_if.description: Declarative skip conditions. An authenticated delivery matching any condition (entries are ORed) is SKIPPED: answered immediately, recorded as a first-class run with status 'skipped' naming the matched condition, and given NO container (no image build, no concurrency slot, no docker run). Keys within one condition are ANDed. A key is a dotted path into the parsed JSON payload ("action", "workflow_run.conclusion", array elements by numeric index) or a request header via the "header:" prefix ("header:x-github-event", name case-insensitive). Comparisons are over stringified scalar leaves (numbers as their JSON literal, true/false/null as those words); objects/arrays are not leaves, and a missing path does not match — evaluation is total and fails toward running the hook. Evaluated only AFTER authentication. Malformed conditions (unknown operator, non-compiling regex, empty condition) are a load/validation error.

state.description: When true, opt the hook into the persistent KV store. The runner injects HOOK_KV_URL (http://localhost:9002) and HOOK_KV_TOKEN (a per-hook bearer token whose namespace is this hook's ID), and a proxy shim entrypoint, so the hook reaches the state API at a plain localhost URL with any HTTP client (no networking, no published port). The hook's data persists across its runs and across server restarts, isolated from other hooks. Default: false (no KV access).

synchronous.description: When true, the server holds the HTTP response open until the container exits. Default: false (returns 202 immediately).

tests.description: Test commands for the hook's scripts. Each entry is an argv array that `webhook-runner test` runs in the hook's built image, so tests exercise exactly the baked code (copy test files into the image and set WORKDIR so relative paths resolve). Tests run without the hook's env, secrets, or payload and must be self-contained; they never run when the hook is triggered.

timeout.description: Go duration for the container timeout (e.g. "5m", "30s"): the absolute processing ceiling, counted from container launch regardless of output. Omit for no absolute ceiling; pair with idle_timeout so a hung run still dies (a hook that omits both runs until it exits).

user.description: User/UID to run the container as (--user flag).

workdir.description: Working directory inside the container (--workdir flag).
